This appears to be a CBP ruling on a microphone cover for aviation headsets (likely Lightspeed or similar). The item is a pouch of foam-backed synthetic leather that fits over a microphone. It is a part or accessory of a headset microphone, so the question is whether it falls under 8518.90 (parts of microphones, headphones, etc.).

Heading 8518 covers microphones and their stands, headphones, earphones, and combined microphone/speaker sets. Subheading 8518.90 covers parts. The statistical suffix for 8518.90.80 is "other", giving 8518.90.8000, which is the commonly used code for parts of headphones and microphones.

Alternatively, the item could be classified as an article of synthetic leather under 4202 or 3926. However, because it is dedicated to the microphone and acts as a baffle, it is more likely a part of the microphone. Heading 8518 is the more probable result. I recall CBP rulings on "windscreens for microphones" classifying them under 8518.90.80.

The 10-digit code would be 8518.90.8000. Subheading 8518.90.80 covers "other" parts, and the statistical suffix is 00 for this entry, so the code is 8518.90.8000.
